images.title: Each value counts as often as it occurs
images.purpose: Shows the core of the frequency table practice: each value is multiplied by its frequency, the products are added, and the total is shared over all the values.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. One short number line in the centre with three stacks of dots, a small product under each stack and the mean marked on the line.
images.exact_structure: A horizontal number line from 1 to 5 with 5 ticks; only 2, 3 and 4 are numbered. Teal (#0072B2) dots stacked above the line: 3 dots at 2, 2 dots at 3, 1 dot at 4, which is 6 dots in all. Under the numbers, one small amber (#E69F00) label per stack: 2 × 3 under 2, 3 × 2 under 3, 4 × 1 under 4. A reddish purple (#CC79A7) triangle touches the line at about 2.67, two thirds of the way from 2 to 3, labelled mean about 2.67. On the right, the line 16 ÷ 6 in dark text. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Multiply each value by how often it occurs, add, then divide by how many values there are.
images.description: Shows the core of the frequency table practice: each value is multiplied by its frequency, the products are added, and the total is shared over all the values.
images.context: 6 + 6 + 4 = 16 over 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 values, mean 2.67. Illustrative small table for the tool.
images.teaching_notes: Links to the cycle rides dot plot question: a dot plot is a frequency table drawn.

image_decisions.why: Stacked dots turn a frequency table into heights, so value times frequency becomes something a child can count.
